paper.title: MotionPyramid: Hierarchical Motion Representation and Residual Interfaces
paper.source_version: arXiv v1, submitted 2026-06-15; versioned PDF SHA-256 acdac8bc5fe63e2abce0dc7a86e3d7cab01ddd1cb42eb10c0fb33531ef0b03dc; no public code or project repository linked in v1; inspected 2026-08-30

decision_relevance.why_admitted: It provides a source-located hierarchy of closed-loop temporal motion interfaces and a controlled speed-versus-precision evaluation. This sharpens how Sam could parameterize reference-oracle timescales and, more importantly, where the fixed action/controller boundary must be enforced.
not_evidence_for: A reference-oracle improvement under Sam's fixed controller and action interface
A task-reward improvement or automated reward-design method
An OGMP state machine or composition of immutable reference trajectories
Human-language steering or a recursive agentic harness
Statistically resolved downstream gains across random seeds

mechanisms.name: Recursive hierarchical action representation
mechanisms.description: Three 32-dimensional latent levels recursively decode across one, five, and ten simulator-step horizons into a 69-dimensional motor command; child decoding is conditioned on current proprioception.

mechanisms.name: Bottom-up closed-loop distillation
mechanisms.description: A motion-tracking teacher supervises the first decoder; each higher decoder reconstructs lower-level latent blocks while previously learned decoders remain frozen, and rollout losses are evaluated on student-visited states.

mechanisms.name: Fixed residual latent interface
mechanisms.description: A downstream policy predicts a residual around a proprioception-conditioned prior mean at one selected pyramid level; the latent unfolds through frozen decoders for that level's native duration.

mechanisms.name: Mixture of Interfaces
mechanisms.description: An SMDP policy jointly selects a horizon from one, five, or ten steps and a 32-dimensional residual latent, exposing online allocation of policy decision bandwidth.

mechanisms.name: Nested Residual Interfaces
mechanisms.description: High-, middle-, and low-level latent commands coexist: frozen parent decoders provide base commands and learned residual heads refine them at ten-, five-, and one-step refresh intervals.

mechanisms.name: Multiscale latent editing probe
mechanisms.description: Latent interpolation, local edits under fixed coarse context, transitions, and fused behaviors qualitatively probe reuse across temporal levels; they do not change training and are not a quantitative composition benchmark.

failure_modes.name: Coarse-interface precision loss
failure_modes.description: The z3 interface is smoothest under the reported tracking metric but drops to 81.0% success and 181.0 mm global MPJPE, showing that temporal compression can discard fine tracking information.

failure_modes.name: Narrow simulated downstream evaluation
failure_modes.description: Downstream evaluation covers three simulated tasks—speed, reach, and strike—not dexterous, long-horizon, or real-world robot behavior.

failure_modes.name: Missing seed uncertainty
failure_modes.description: The main downstream curves omit seed error bars because of computational cost, so run-to-run variability is unquantified.

failure_modes.name: Manually selected hierarchy
failure_modes.description: The number of levels, horizons 1/5/10, and residual routing rules are specified by hand rather than learned or broadly swept.

failure_modes.name: Qualitative-only composition evidence
failure_modes.description: Interpolation, transition, and composition demos are representation probes without quantitative benchmarks, independent trials, or uncertainty.

failure_modes.name: Fixed-trainer contract mismatch
failure_modes.description: Using MotionPyramid directly replaces raw actions with learned latent interfaces and changes decision timing, PPO storage, and likelihood evaluation; it cannot be admitted as an oracle-only or reward-only intervention under Sam's initial contract.

failure_modes.name: Implementation and checkpoint pin gap
failure_modes.description: v1 links no official code, repository, or checkpoint digest, and reports using the latest available checkpoint for long-running figures unless otherwise specified.

evaluation.name: Controlled action-interface comparison
evaluation.description: For downstream RL, task reward, observations, architecture, optimizer, initial-state distribution, and training budget are held fixed while the action interface changes.

evaluation.name: AMASS-Train fixed-interface tracking
evaluation.description: Table 2 measures rollout success, global MPJPE, global/local rotation error, and normalized joint-motion smoothness across raw, z1, z2, and z3 interfaces.

evaluation.name: Unguided prior-sampling regularity
evaluation.description: Across 256 ten-second rollouts per level, the paper measures path distance, speed, action variation, minimum root height, and low-root collapse counts without downstream task reward.

evaluation.name: Speed, reach, and strike downstream tasks
evaluation.description: The tasks probe locomotion, target alignment, and contact timing; paper figures report the nested Residual Interfaces as strongest overall, but main curves lack seed error bars.

evaluation.name: Multiscale editing probes
evaluation.description: Traversal, interpolation, transition, and qualitative composition inspect editable latent directions across temporal levels; these probes are illustrative rather than benchmarked.

evidence.locator: arXiv abstract page, submission history; versioned PDF https://arxiv.org/pdf/2606.20705v1
evidence.claim: MotionPyramid v1 was submitted 15 June 2026 by Gao Zhu, Zaishuo Xia, and Yubei Chen; the downloaded versioned PDF has SHA-256 acdac8bc5fe63e2abce0dc7a86e3d7cab01ddd1cb42eb10c0fb33531ef0b03dc.

evidence.locator: Section 2, opening and Section 2.2, especially hierarchy definition and recursive unfolding
evidence.claim: Three latent levels recursively decode 32-dimensional commands at horizons 1, 5, and 10 to a 69-dimensional motor command at 30, 6, and 3 Hz; child-boundary decoding reads current proprioception.
A motion-tracking teacher supervises sequential bottom-up decoder training, with lower decoders frozen and distillation evaluated on states visited by the learned interface.

evidence.locator: Section 2.4, equations for p_l and residual action
evidence.claim: Downstream fixed-interface policies output residuals around frozen proprioception-conditioned prior means, and PPO likelihood is computed over the residual.
Mixture of Interfaces jointly samples a level from {1,2,3} and a same-dimension residual latent, then executes the selected frozen decoder path for its native horizon.

Nested Residual Interfaces refresh z3, z2, and z1 residuals every 10, 5, and 1 steps; all pretrained decoders and priors remain frozen while downstream actor, critic, and residual heads are optimized.

evidence.locator: Section 3.2, controlled-comparison paragraph and Figure 2 discussion
evidence.claim: For downstream RL, comparisons hold task reward, observation space, policy architecture, optimizer, initial-state distribution, and training budget fixed while changing the action interface.

AMASS-Train tracking reports success, global MPJPE, global/local rotation errors, and normalized smoothness for scratch/raw, z1, z2, and z3, including z3 81.0% success, 181.0 mm global MPJPE, and 229.2 smoothness cost.
Prior sampling uses 256 ten-second rollouts per level and reports path distance, speed, action change, minimum root height, and low-root counts under a 0.15 m proxy threshold.

evidence.locator: Section 3.4, Figures 1 and 5, and Appendix A.11
evidence.claim: Interpolation, transition, and composition examples are presented as qualitative representation probes; Appendix A.11 states that the probe does not change the training objective.
The paper limits downstream evaluation to three simulated tasks, omits seed error bars on main curves, manually specifies horizons 1/5/10, and treats editing/composition results as qualitative.

PPO uses gamma 0.99, GAE lambda 0.95, clip 0.2, gradient clip 50, observation clip [-5,5], 32-step rollouts, six epochs, separate 2048/1024/512 MLPs, and tabulated learning rates/log standard deviations.
Decoder training uses 32-dimensional latents, a 3e-5 learning rate, specified MLP widths, level-specific KL schedules, and AR(1) regularization with weight 0.005 and phi 0.99.

evidence.locator: Section 3.1 and Appendix B, final experiment paragraph
evidence.claim: Pretraining uses 11,314 AMASS clips; speed, reach, and strike use 512 parallel environments with task-specific target schedules.
Temporally extended interfaces induce an SMDP and require duration-aware reward accumulation, discounts, GAE, PPO likelihoods at decision boundaries, and one stored transition per latent decision.

Experiments use an eight-RTX-4090 workstation, PyTorch 2.7, CUDA 12.8, and Isaac Lab; downstream runs use four GPUs, and long-running figures use the latest available checkpoint unless otherwise stated.
The paper names AMASS, Isaac Lab, and PyTorch and states what any released code will include, but v1 does not identify a code repository, project page, release, commit, or checkpoint artifact.
